correctness.rationale: The difference Y−X has normalized covariogram density g(z)/A_n², and the width-one body has circular difference body, so the endpoint probability integrates G_n(s)=∫g((1−s)uθ)dθ radially over s∈(0,ε). There are 2n oriented corner–arc sectors of width α=π/n. In an interior angular sector the two tangent rays at the corner give simplex coefficient c(φ)=sin α/[2 sinφ sin(α−φ)]=(cotφ+cot(α−φ))/2. The trim δ_s=√s log(1/s) enforces uniform O(1/log²(1/s)) relative curvature error; nonincident disks have slack on this trim. Endpoint overlap is bounded by C min(s^(3/2),s²/Δ), giving an o(s² log(1/s)) integrated contribution. Exact integral of c over each trimmed sector is ½log(1/s)+lower order, so G_n(s)~n s²log(1/s), and radial integration gives n/(3A_n²)ε³log(1/ε). Independently checked trig identity and direct small-s local lens geometry for n=3,5; e.g. local coefficient target √3 ≈1.73205 versus s=0.003 numerical 1.71906 for n=3, convergence corroboration only. Disk comparator coefficient independently follows from circle-lens asymptotic. The theorem fixes n first and makes no n-uniform limit assertion.

Numerical local lens checks alone do not establish the logarithmic asymptotic; analytic trimmed estimates provide proof.

Falcó–Myroshnychenko covers area/symmetry minimizers, Pure et al straight-edge polygon pair distances, Bonnet et al mean distance bounds; the published regular Reuleaux Estermann primary result concerns area-ratio symmetry, not the two-point covariogram endpoint. The general covariogram identity and corner contact geometry are classical; novel asserted content is the sharp ε³log(1/ε) law and coefficient n/(3A_n²). This best-of-knowledge result carries residual risk of an unindexed general corner–arc covariogram theorem.
